facility_roles.quote: The Spherical Neutral Detector (SND) [2,3] is a facility for high energy physics experiments. It has been mounted at the VEPP-2M e+e- collider in Novosibirsk, Russia.

summary.plain: The Spherical Neutral Detector at the Budker Institute in Novosibirsk, a ball of 1,632 sodium iodide crystals around the collision point. It ran at VEPP-2M from 1995 to 2000, was upgraded and has run at VEPP-2000 since 2010, measuring how electron-positron collisions at 0.4-2 GeV make photons and hadrons.
summary.technical: SND: three-layer spherical NaI(Tl) calorimeter of 1632 crystals (13.5 radiation lengths, 3.6 t), cylindrical drift chambers inside and a muon/veto system of streamer tubes and scintillators outside; VEPP-2M (0.7-1.4 GeV) 1995-2000, upgraded after 2000 for VEPP-2000, operating there since 2010; successor of the ND neutral detector (1982-87).
